reviews.review: Played 5 hours so far - it's every bit as good as these reviews imply. Get this game.
R O C K   A N D   R O L L   A N D   S T O N E ! ! !

Easily one of the most entertaining co-op games I've played in the last five years. Dripping with character from top to bottom. Each class is completely unique, using different tools to traverse the procedurally-generated terrain and different weapons to carve through enemies. The four classes are also fully customizable, including weapon loadouts, armor bonuses, secondary weapon types, and overclocks. There are seven different mission types and ten different biomes, each with their own unique hazards, benefits and pitfalls. "Mutations" can also occur on missions, presenting a different kind of challenges or benefits such as extra damage from enemies, extra weak point damage on all enemies, or spawning a giant immortal exploding death ball that slowly follows you through the mission. Five difficulty settings means the game can also be as podcast-listeningly easy or as keyboard-smashingly frustrating as you want. Increasing the difficulty increases the payout of both money and minerals, so feel free to amp up the risk for a greater reward.

Do missions to earn resources. Use resources to buy upgrades for your weapons and cosmetics for your class. Doing anything will earn you perk points. Spend these on perks for meta bonuses like the ability to carry more minerals or the ability to charm the native fauna and have it follow you around helping out in fights. Grab flowers to make special beer. The house beer offers you a buff for your next mission. Other beer gets you drunk, which persists through your next mission. Tired of running random missions? Pick up an assignment. Earn yourself some more dosh. Earn enough levels to unlock more assignments, like picking up more weapon types for your dwarves. Dwarf's at cap? Play another class while you do the assignment to get him promoted. Promoting your dwarf means you can start getting Matrix Cores. With enough money and minerals, they turn into overclocks for your weapons or unique cosmetics for the miners. What's an overclock? Well, that's a weapon-specific upgrade that can offer a small tweak, like increasing your rate of fire, or a large one, like turning your grenade launcher's ammo into nukes. Bored of regular missions? Or maybe you're kitted out and want a bigger challenge? Why not try a Deep Dive? Deep Dives are three regular missions stapled together that increase in difficulty with each step. Sounds too easy? Try an Elite Deep Dive! Same thing but insanely harder. Finish one in under 45 minutes and you get a neat achievement.

Play alone and go adventuring with Bosco, your fully-customizable helper drone. You can order him to shine lights on those hard to see places, dig through dirt walls, grab minerals out of walls, or blast enemies with his rocket launcher. He also helps you fight and can even resurrect you when you go down. If you get lonely, you can play with friends or strangers online. A full team opens up a whole slew of options for mobility and battle tactics, or can speed up a mission by splitting up to cover more ground. The procedurally generated environments and modular challenge coupled with the developers' propensity for releasing free content patches means the game has virtually infinite replayability. Definitely a must-buy at the price tag of $30.
